poster.headline: WHAT TRULY DRIVES CONTRACEPTIVE UPTAKE?
poster.subheadline: Real-World Evidence from 419 Women of Reproductive Age in Mkuranga District
poster.intro: In this cross-sectional study of 419 women, modern contraceptive prevalence was 25.1%. Using Modified Poisson regression (Zou 2004) to avoid Odds Ratio inflation, we evaluated independent knowledge and socio-cultural determinants.
poster.author_role: MD Candidate @ MUHAS | Data Analyst | Founder @ Tafiti99

body.title: MODIFIED POISSON REGRESSION: INDEPENDENT PREDICTORS (aPR)
rows: Male approval independently boosts use by 85%
Married / Cohabiting vs. Not in union

body.title: THREE CRITICAL LESSONS FOR CLINICIANS & RESEARCHERS

items.title: 1. ENGAGE PARTNERS ACTIVELY
items.text: Partner communication and approval were the single strongest drivers of modern contraceptive uptake (aPR up to 2.67). Interventions must engage couples rather than treating family planning as female-only.

items.title: 2. TARGET HIGH-PARITY BARRIERS
items.text: Women with 3 or more children showed 32% lower use despite having achieved family size goals. Reproductive health services must proactively target misconceptions and fatigue in multiparous women.

items.title: 3. USE MODIFIED POISSON IN R
items.text: Because prevalence was 25.1% (>10%), logistic regression Odds Ratios would severely overestimate true risk. Modified Poisson regression (log-link + sandwich::vcovHC) guarantees valid Prevalence Ratios.
